newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures surge to new high on CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures surge to new high on CPI.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures resumed their upward march, climbing to their second record high in two days this morning on tame June inflation data.
The consumer price index inched up 0.1 percent in June, with core inflation excluding food and energy also rising just 0.1 percent. Analysts had forecast a gain of 0.2 percent in both readings.
June Treasury bond futures soared nearly 1/2 point on the news, propeling S&P 500 stock index futures to a new all-time high in electronic trading on Globex.
"Bonds rallied off the CPI numbers, and the (S&Ps) are just going along for the ride," said one stock index floor trader.
September S&P 500 futures vaulted above the old contract high of 934.00 set Tuesday and extended the move to a new all-time peak of 937.60 after the opening of pit trading.
Stock index traders said the ability of the Dow Jones Industrial Average to pierce 8,000 provided psychological support.
The Dow reached 8,003 in early trading before edging back and was last trading up 20 points at 7996.

The Nasdaq composite index continued to power higher, following the release of Intel Corp earnings after Tuesday's close. The company said second quarter net income rose to $0.92 per share, compared with $0.59 in the same period a yaer ago.
The September Nasdaq futures contract continued to make new highs this morning and was last trading up about 29 points at 1097.

S&P 500 futures were up 7.75 points at 939.40, Nasdaq 100s rose 28.75 to 1097.00, Russell 2000s were up 2.20 points at 413.25, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 360.0 to 20,535.0 and Midcap 400s rose 1.80 points to 306.60.
